minutes.headline: Water commissioners favored expanded master plan study and grant applications; funding options and approval set for next meeting.
minutes.summary: Consulting engineers presented a proposed expansion of the water master plan: treating the Keating well, interconnecting with neighboring systems, and possible new sources. Board members discussed pilot-test results on hardness removal, how to fund the work through grants or the town meeting, and the plan to bring a revised proposal to the next full board meeting. The board also took up the audit engagement letter, a per-unit charge for the Mass project, and replacing the dump truck.

votes.motion: Motion to approve the minutes of August 14th.
Motion to allow the acting chair to sign the engagement letter for the annual audit.

budget_items.what_was_said: A board member referred to the proposed spending for the study; it would need a vote at town meeting.
The engineers discussed a rolling state revolving fund application covering planning and past reimbursements, with an example of one grant request.
The district submitted its costs so far; it expects a first-round amount and further rounds.
The auditor's fee was said to be roughly level over two years and the board judged it not worth rebidding.

The charge on bills starting in October was discussed as per unit rather than per account, so the average would be lower. Commercial and sprinkler rates were deferred until the final bond number is known.
Engineers described recent bids as varying widely depending on timing.
The board discussed replacing the old dump truck with a larger one and asked for prices.

decisions.decision: Engineers to send a revised proposal before the next full board meeting, in two weeks, including added scope on updating costs.
Engineers to give funding options at the next meeting; the board will decide on funding and the grant.
Board leaned toward dropping the full optional hydraulic model, with only a high-level comparison of neighboring systems.
Staff to get prices on a larger replacement truck and make recommendations.
Keep the per-unit charge at the originally announced amount for now and revisit once the final bond number is known.
